title: Live Spectrum Display Bin Averaging
description: A simulated 128x64 OLED spectrum above the full 256-bin reference, with shaded bands showing which bins average into each displayed bar.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Spectrum Display
Embedded Systems
chapter_title: Computing and Displaying a Real Spectrum

learningObjectives: Examine how display bar count relates to underlying bin count
Compare averaging behavior across different signal shapes
Explain why averaging flattens narrow peaks
prerequisites: An FFT produces a magnitude per bin

controls.label: Next simulated frame
controls.purpose: Cycle through single tone, chord, and white noise

simulationModel.modelType: Group-mean downsampling of a fixed spectrum
equations: bar value = mean of its group of bins
assumptions: Bar counts are powers of two so groups divide evenly
Example spectra are precomputed and deterministic
limitations: Uses group mean; many real displays use group maximum, which preserves peak height and is discussed in the documentation

keyQuestions: Why is the peak shorter on the OLED than in the reference?
Which signal shape survives heavy averaging best?
commonMisconceptions: That a shorter averaged bar means less energy is present
That more display bars always improves the display
assessmentOpportunities: Judge whether two tones a given number of bins apart remain separable
